correctness.rationale: For each unequal diagonal-color pair the commutator equation uniquely determines one radical coordinate; for each equal pair it leaves a free radical coordinate and may identify two diagonal labels. Thus the exact dimension equals the number of equal pairs plus the number of components of the nonzero-arrow equality graph. Conditional color graphs are independent dense bipartite Bernoulli graphs; a cut union bound gives exponential connectedness when color counts are linear, itself exponentially likely. Independent multinomial CLTs and the exact cancellation of linear occupancy terms give the Gaussian-product limit and its characteristic function. Direct commutator-rank and partner-enumeration checks reproduced small cases.

value.rationale: The size of the commutant is a natural multiplicative-algebra invariant. The exact identity reduces centralizer enumeration in an infinite family of radical-square-zero incidence algebras to a random-graph component statistic, and the non-Gaussian n-scale law quantifies its genuinely non-normal fluctuations. The algebra is the complete bipartite height-two incidence algebra, motivated independently of the numerical answer and extending published single-edge triangular results.
